title: Give every carrier's rate card the same checks and its own rates

blocks.text: The shop ships with several carriers, and each carrier's rates come from a slow lookup: a carrier's API, or a file. `Shipping.CachedRateCard` is the base class for them, and `Shipping.ParcelPost` is the first carrier. The freight team will add theirs next month, as their own subclass, and the last time they did, two things went wrong: their card was created with the currency `"usd"`, and every invoice it produced was refused by the bank; and once both carriers had quoted the same zone, the checkout page showed Parcel Post's price for freight.
Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Shipping.java`, both in `CachedRateCard`:

items: the constructor: no carrier's card, today's or one written later, can exist with a currency that isn't an ISO 4217 code (three capital letters); refuse one with `IllegalArgumentException`;
`rateCents(zone)`: the card's rate for the zone, looking each zone up at most once for that card.

blocks.text: About six lines in total. The tests add a carrier of their own, the way the freight team will.

cases.says: Parcel Post quotes the rates of its table, in its currency, and refuses a currency that isn't three capital letters
a carrier's card looks each zone up once, however often the zone is asked for
a carrier written later, as its own subclass with its own constructor, still can't be created with a currency that isn't an ISO code
two carriers asked for the same zone each answer with their own rate

origin.section: An Abstract Class Can't Be Instantiated, but Its Constructor Runs for Every Subclass

concepts: An abstract class can't be instantiated, but its constructor runs for every subclass, anonymous ones included, so the checks every subclass needs go there.
Every field of an interface is public static final, so a mutable object declared there is one shared value for every implementation, and per-object state needs an abstract class.
